findings.claim: The requirement asks for all generated code to carry `ExcludeFromCodeCoverage`, but every template wraps the attribute in `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`. Projects targeting netstandard2.0 or any .NET Framework TFM therefore get undecorated formatters and resolvers. The attribute is available on both: netstandard2.0 exposes `System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute`, and .NET Framework 4.0+ has it in mscorlib with AttributeUsage that includes Class. So the derived criterion ('the attribute must exist there or be conditionally emitted') does not justify excluding these targets. netstandard2.0 is the most common library target, so a large share of users get no benefit.

receipt_plan.detail: Run tests/MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Tests/Receipts/ExcludeFromCodeCoverageTfmTests.cs. With the NETSTANDARD2_0 or NETFRAMEWORK preprocessor symbol set, generated formatter and resolver classes have no active ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute, so the test fails on head. As a second check, compile a netstandard2.0 class library carrying `[System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]` on a class: it builds with no error, which shows the guard is unnecessary.

findings.claim: The README says the attribute 'is only emitted for targets where it is available (not `netstandard2.0` or .NET Framework)'. This is factually wrong: `ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute` exists in netstandard2.0 and in .NET Framework 4.0+. The docs misstate why those targets are left out of the requirement.

receipt_plan.detail: Check the netstandard2.0 reference assembly (NETStandard.Library 2.0 ref/netstandard.dll) and the .NET Framework 4.x mscorlib for System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute. It is present in both, which contradicts README.md:1639-1640.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Always on, with no setting. Every formatter template (object, string-key, enum, union) and every resolver template (resolver, composite resolver, and their FormatterCache/GetFormatterHelper nested classes) emits `[global::System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]` unconditionally from the generator. No option is added, and users cannot turn it off.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: On by default, with an opt-out setting, which the requirement explicitly calls acceptable. Add a boolean option (for example `ExcludeFromCodeCoverage`, default true) to the generator options, read it from the existing option sources such as the analyzer config or MSBuild property. Pass it into the templates and wrap each emitted attribute line in an `if (Options...ExcludeFromCodeCoverage)` template block, then document the opt-out in README.
